150 (x, out from wall) x 20 (y, thick, up) x 200 (z, wide) mm
Steel stated; E 210 GPa, nu 0.3 standard steel values
6 kN downward (-y) spread uniformly over whole top face y=20; ~1.3% on wall-edge nodes goes straight into the support, as for a real uniform pressure

final:
The cantilevered slab spec is built and passes validation with no errors. The render shows the fixed wall face at x = 0 and the 6 kN load on the top face, as the brief describes.

- **Domain:** 150 × 20 × 200 mm (x out from the wall, y up, z across the width). At 2 mm elements that is a 75 × 10 × 100 grid, or 75,000 elements.
- **Material:** steel, using the standard values E = 210,000 N/mm² and ν = 0.3. The volume fraction is 0.3.
- **Support:** the whole wall face (x = 0) is fixed in x, y and z, which covers 1,111 nodes.
- **Load:** 6,000 N downward (−y), shared equally across all 7,676 nodes on the top face (y = 20).

Validation gave one warning: about 1.3% of the load lands on the top-face nodes along the wall edge, which are fixed, so that share goes straight into the support. A uniform load on a real slab behaves the same way at the wall, so I left it as is.

Every item is tagged stated (units, domain, material, volume fraction, resolution, support and load), and none are untagged or assumed, so I didn't need to ask any questions.

DONE. No assumptions beyond the standard steel properties (E = 210 GPa, ν = 0.3) and expressing 6 kN as 6,000 N in mm/N units.
